page: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is a memory-optimized and storage-capable virtual machine belonging to the Lasv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 3.7 GHz and features 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core.

For local storage, the instance includes 1920 GB of bundled capacity and is Premium Storage capable. It does not feature any integrated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16, alongside cryptographic accelerations like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks (256MB) is weak, registering at 38.85 GB/sec. Multi-core execution, database operations, and web serving throughput fall into the average tier, with Redis SET operations achieving 11.75 million operations per second. This hardware profile is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, and text processing tasks that benefit from high local storage capacity and strong single-thread performance.
description: Microsoft Azure L8as_v4 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Lasv4 family, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores), 64.0 GB of system memory, and 1920 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server supports advanced vector and cryptographic instructions such as AVX512 and VAES. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, though large-block memory bandwidth is relatively weak. Multi-core processing, database operations, and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier. Lacking integrated GPUs, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, and text processing tasks requiring substantial local storage without the need for hardware acceleration.
